newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Resources weigh on Australian stocks at open.
newsitem.headline: Resources weigh on Australian stocks at open.

text.p: The Australian share market edged slightly lower at the open on Thursday, a sagging resource sector just outweighing a marginally firmer industrials sector.
From the opening, the All Ordinaries index fell 1.4 points to 2,244.9. The September share price index futures fell three points to 2,246, a 1.1 point premium to the underlying index.
Brokers said while a buoyant banking sector bolstered the industrials grouping, base metals prices that continued to weaken in offshore markets had generated resources selling.
"BHP and CRA have led the miners down again, but overall its been fairly steady," said a Sydney broker.
"Banks are performing well again and that is holding the whole market."
Of the banks, Commonwealth Bank continued to star with demand for its high-yielding, partly paid instalment receipts the impetus although all the major banks were stronger.
Expectations were for a rangebound day in the absence of major shocks from August employment data.

"It's been in a narrow range so far. The jobs data may give a push later on but as to which way who knows?" the broker said. Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about seven to six, while about 45 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
